title: Feeding T75, T150, and 6wp Backup
author: Andrea Argouarch
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8gkhtuw

steps.title: Turn off UV and clean hood
steps.instruction: Switch off the UV lights in the biosafety cabinet and wipe the interior surfaces with 70 % ethanol.

steps.title: Prepare sterile media in hood
steps.instruction: Wipe all items with 70 % ethanol, then bring into the hood sterile filtered DMEM high‑glucose pyruvate (Thermo Fisher Catalog #11995073) supplemented with Penicillin‑Streptomycin (Gibco, Catalog #15140122) and Fetal Bovine Serum (VWR International, Catalog #97068‑091).

steps.title: Observe cell morphology
steps.instruction: Examine the cultures for cell morphology and outgrowth under the microscope.

steps.title: Add media to flasks
steps.instruction: Dispense the prepared media with penicillin‑streptomycin into the appropriate vessels.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 mL of media to the T75 flask.
Add 2 mL of media to the 6‑well plate backup.

steps.title: Feed cultures regularly
steps.instruction: Replace media every 2–3 days and continue feeding until cultures reach 90–100 % confluence.

steps.title: Clean hood and reactivate UV
steps.instruction: Wipe the biosafety cabinet with 70 % ethanol, then turn the UV lights back on to sterilize.

steps.title: Add media to T150 flask
steps.instruction: Add 30 mL of the prepared media with penicillin‑streptomycin to the T150 flask.
